method: Successful authorized current-draft queries; self-hits excluded; top three other candidates read in full. Later duplicate candidate circle_newcomer is tracked once in its own story batch.

cards.assessment: Two friends who dislike each other have each saved the player a seat; the decision is partiality versus mediation. The awkward matchmaking supper, fame-driven competition for access, and house-versus-strangers seating have different conflicts and payoffs.
Relaying angry messages verbatim versus softening them differs from carrying an apology/gift, delivering a romantic note, and reconciling a completed falling-out through a meeting.

The player witnesses a dispute between two other claimants. The fame-scandal card concerns credit the player wrongly received; the professor example concerns accidental success, and the laboratory card concerns uncooperative partners. Shared classroom credit is not the same viewpoint and decision.

Witnessing one known classmate hex another's boots creates a truth-versus-cover-up choice. Reflect concerns defending against an ambush, the stairs steal the player's shoe, and Kael intimidates bullies. No repeated decision/punchline.

A friend asks the player to stop bringing a mutual enemy. Fame-wedge instead warns about an opportunist exploiting access; circling concerns a possible romance; couple-bubble concerns being left out by two close friends. The relationship triangle alone is not a duplicate.

An ashamed sender cannot face delivering an apology/gift. The closest note cards concern romance or escalating hostile messages; the parcel is a home gift to the player. Their reasons and decisions differ.

A serious grudge duel between two known friends asks for seconding or mediation. The hall card is a practice bout with second/referee options; the garden card is a strangers' honour duel requiring legal witnessing or a ward; Thorne's is a faculty rivalry and invitation. Similar seconding device, different conflict, agency and relationship stakes.

A tied common-room vote requires siding with a faction or proposing a compromise. The nearest cards compete for a chair or warm niche as individuals, or pit the player against Lyra over a library seat. No group-vote scene repeats.

Three classmates cannot brew together because two feud. The stirring-count, self-stirring cauldron and fire/water kettle lessons instead test technique or machinery; they do not ask the player to reconcile feuding partners.

Two friends admit the player to their private drawn cipher at the cost of lecture attention. Passing study notes, learning roof-safety marks and receiving forbidden-section notes/key have different purposes, access and consequences.

The player chooses how to enter two friends' private joke. Brask assesses storytelling, the Season homecoming concerns fame-driven estrangement, and an impression/skit tests the player's response to public parody. A joke motif alone does not duplicate the choice.

Impersonating an absent student during roll call differs from taking blame for contraband, editing a prefect ledger during detention, and clearing a classmate with a reluctant witness. Different deception, audience and promised consequence.

The study-circle newcomer is a substantive overlapping exclusion/admission scene, and is being reviewed as the later duplicate candidate under circle_newcomer. The saved-seat cards concern choosing between existing invitations rather than excluding an unwanted newcomer. No duplicate-repair request is issued twice for the same pair.

Two friends invite the player out from bed for a three-person rooftop night; the decision is joining them or keeping a night's rest. The partner roof card trades intimacy versus a shorter date, midnight stars is observatory stargazing, and Starfall at home is a family festival. Shared roofs/stars/late nights are noted; no blocking complete-premise repeat established.

Reconciling two established friends who each demand loyalty differs from the torn-book accusation/truth problem, a meal-time seating feud and fame-driven competing friendship claims. The new findings concern the dishonest meeting invitations, not a duplicated conflict.
